newsitem.title: USA: IMF backs Philippines' move to flexible rates.
newsitem.headline: IMF backs Philippines' move to flexible rates.

text.p: IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday he welcomed action taken less than an hour earlier by the Philippines Central Bank to allow greater peso exchange rate flexibility.
"The management of the IMF strongly commends the Philippine authorities for their timely and decisive action," Camdessus said in a statement.

Importantly, Camdessus said he would recommend that the IMF board approve the Philippines' request for an extension of its Extended Fund Facility -- set to expire on July 23, 1997 -- and that he would ask the board to make additional borrowing authority available.

"I will recommend to the IMF Board that it make available additional financial resources on which the Philippines could draw to support their comprehensive strategy to safeguard macroeconomic stability," he said.

Early on Friday in Manila, the Philippines Central Bank said it would allow the peso to move in a wider range against the U.S. dollar. The move follows pressure on the peso after the Thai government devalued its baht currency on July 2.
The peso tumbled to 29.45 per dollar at the start of Asian trade on Friday from 26.40 at Thursday's close and minutes later the Bankers Association of the Philippines temporarily halted dealings.
Traders there reportedly said the Philippine central bank's announcement was equivalent to a devaluation of the currency.

"I am confident that this set of measures, in conjunction with the authorities' resolve to maintain fiscal and monetary discipline, will help protect the Philippine economy from the consequences of instability in regional financial markets," Camdessus said.
IMF spokesman David Hawley declined to give further details but did say the Fund's statement "is a response to an announcement by the Philippine authorities".
